how: One claim, four graphs

A nanopublication is one claim small enough to be wrong on its own: an assertion, where it came from, who published it, and a head naming the other three. The validator either accepts the record or it does not.
The test that matters
Find the one sentence a reader could quote. If it is true of the finding AND states the finding's limit, the record is honest. If the limit only exists in your head, it is not.
What a pass means

Exit 0 with an empty `unexpected` list. Three complaints are allowed by name on an unsigned draft — no signature, no template, a temp graph URI — and the allowance list is in source with a written reason.
uses: built
Distil a book into citable claims
Darwin, Thompson, Wolfram and Turing were read into claims, each traced to its source passage, and the claim graph is browsable.
built
Publish a negative result
Several records in the repo exist to say a thing did NOT hold — a retracted link, a refuted textbook claim, a null that was contradicted and withdrawn.
partial
Let an outside agent submit evidence
The format and the checker are real and run. Signing and publishing to the production registry need a key owner's approval, which is a human decision and deliberately not automated.
community: Bring a claim, not an opinion
The unit of contribution is one small claim with its locator. That is a low bar to clear and a hard one to fake, which is the point.
Disagreement has an address
Two people who disagree end up pointing at the same record and arguing about its evidence rather than about what was meant.
Negative results are first-class
A record that says "this did not hold" counts the same as one that says it did. Most venues cannot say that.

open.lead: Questions about the record format itself, still open in this repo.

how: Two gates
A claim becomes an axiom only if it compiles in Lean 4 AND survives agent debate on the existing evidence. Both, or neither.
The non-vacuity witness
Every law carries concrete numbers that satisfy its hypotheses, proved rather than asserted. A theorem whose hypotheses can never be met is true and worthless.
Load-bearing hypotheses

The checker strips every relational binder and recompiles. If it still compiles, the hypotheses were decorative and the formalisation FAILS. That is the most common silent failure in formalised claims.
uses: built
Settle what a disagreement is about
Several arguments in this repo turned out to be about what follows from what, not about the world. Formalising separates the two, and the open-questions ledger records which is which.
built
Catch a claim that proves nothing
The hypothesis-stripping check has refused formalisations that compiled cleanly. Compiling is not the bar.
proposed
Submit your own theorem to the forum
The gates exist and run. An outside submission path — upload, debate, promote — is designed and not built.
community: A proof is reviewable by a machine first
The kernel checks the step before a human spends attention on it, so review time goes to whether the statement says what the claim says.
Debate before promotion
A claim does not become an axiom because it compiled. It has to survive argument about the evidence, and the argument is recorded.
Exemptions are written down
Laws that evaluate nothing against a design are listed with a reason each. Explained is not the same as silent.

open.lead: Biology's open questions, split into the part Lean can settle and the part only measurement can. These are the fourteen the capability map holds; none is answered here.

grand.text: Given a genome, what phenotype does it produce, and why can we not read one off the other?
How does a one-dimensional sequence specify a three-dimensional animal, reliably, at the right size, generation after generation?
Why did replicators become chromosomes, cells become eukaryotes, individuals become societies? What makes a transition in individuality happen, and why so rarely?
When does selection act on the group rather than on the individual, and is the distinction a fact about the world or a choice of bookkeeping?
Does relatedness times benefit exceeding cost explain altruism in general, or only under assumptions that rarely hold?
Does natural selection increase mean fitness at a rate equal to the additive genetic variance in fitness, and if so, under what conditions and in what sense?
A replicator needs an accurate copying machine, and an accurate copying machine needs a long genome, which needs accurate copying. How did the first one get started?
Why does metabolic rate scale with body mass to a power near three-quarters rather than two-thirds, and is there a single exponent at all?
Why does this code, and not one of the million alternatives, map 64 codons onto 20 amino acids?
Is there one explanation of why organisms age, or several processes that happen to coincide?
What makes a lineage able to generate useful variation, and is that capacity itself a product of selection?
Can we say what a population will do next, and if not in detail, then what can we rule out?
What is the smallest set of genes that can make a self-replicating cell, and why those?
Why is an organism the size and shape it is, and how does a form keep its proportions as it grows? This is literally this repository's subject.

ledger.text: What adult mass should stand for a flying fish at standard length 0.203 m: the one specimen the aerodynamics were measured on (0.060 kg), or a typical adult on the population length-weight curve (0.100-0.132 kg)?
What is the sign of the membrane-potential change by which kcnk5b gain of function (the zebrafish alf alleles) drives fin overgrowth, in the tissue where the growth happens?

What fraction of the night does a zebrafish larva spend asleep: 58% or 84%? And is "sleep fraction" a measurable property of the animal at all, independent of the movement criterion used to define it?
Which zebrafish paralogue does the symbol lat4a denote, and which paralogue carries the flying-fish comparative signal?
Which zebrafish genes are "in" a signalling pathway? Four curated sources disagree so strongly that pairwise agreement for Wnt, the best-studied case, is a Jaccard index of only 0.12 to 0.28.

Does the osmolyte mechanism set a depth ceiling for teleost fishes, and where? A hard cap at 8200 m is refuted by a real fish at 8336 m; what remains in question is whether the mechanism sets a ceiling with a deeper constant, or only a soft one with no fixed value.
What is the critical swimming speed of an adult zebrafish at 28 C: about 0.56 m/s or about 0.24 m/s?

how: Tools, not endpoints
The surface was derived from a capability map: who would ask, what they would actually ask, and which of the big open questions it touches.
It declines to guess
Every tool returns a named verdict. `cannot-evaluate` names the input it would need. Supply it and call again, or report the absence — do not substitute a default.
Pinned lawsets
Checks run at a pinned law-set version, so a law released mid-run cannot move a result and any verdict can be reproduced later.
uses: built
Ask what is already known about a claim
One claim id in, its nanopub drafts and evidence out.
built
Check a design against the law registry
The interesting answer is the `cannot-evaluate` rows, each naming the missing input.
partial
Drive the whole pipeline from an agent
The tools exist and are callable. The capability map reports that a large share of the tool references its own use cases need are still MISSING, and does not round that up.
community: Built for named personas
The tool list answers specific people asking specific things, and the map says which questions it cannot answer yet.
The gaps are published
The missing-tool list is part of the product. It is the contribution queue.
Any agent is a first-class caller
The CLI, the API and the MCP server are the same surface, so an agent is not a second-class user of a human tool.

how: Prose to specification
A sentence becomes criteria in SI units. Clauses it cannot parse are reported, never silently dropped.
Down nine layers
From the specification to organ systems, tissues, cells, pathways, genes and developmental time — each layer with its ontology id.
Out as geometry
The design leaves the screen as STL meshes and sequence, which is how it reaches a printer or a wet lab.
uses: proposed
Design Xenobots

The sharpest case for the harness, and NOT because of a genome. A Xenobot has no engineered sequence: it is wild-type Xenopus cells arranged into a shape an evolutionary algorithm searched over. So the design variable is arrangement, and the target function is LOCOMOTION — a phenotype in time. Run one through validation and genotype similarity comes back ~100% and tells you nothing. Only the physics check can adjudicate. Nothing here has been run.
partial
Hybrids, chimeras, and reconstructed ancestors

A two-parent chimera and a parametric weighted-chimera builder exist and run — `ff-zf-chimera` is a real case in the gene diff, built from parents plus labelled deltas. Reconstructing an ANCESTOR is the interesting scientific version and has not been attempted.
built
Find out which data is missing

Arguably the most useful thing it does today. The functional registry states its own poverty in numbers, and the capability map publishes its missing tool references. Pointing at what to collect next is a real output.
community: A design is a shareable object
Specification, mesh and sequence are files. A design can be handed to someone who disagrees with it.
Printable
The kits come out as STL. A disagreement about a shape can be settled on a desk.
Labelled in development
The studio says so on screen. Shipping an honest label beats shipping a confident one.

how: The analogue is CURATED, not searched

This is the thing most readers assume wrongly. There is no search: the nearest functional analogue comes from a hand-written registry of four functions, each with at most two taxa carrying a curated satisfies flag. The pick is a filter and first-in-source-order. No distance metric selects it, no database is queried at run time, and no model is prompted.
Distances are reported, never used to choose
Phylogenetic and functional distance are computed AFTER the choice and never feed back into it. They are reported separately and never combined.
It refuses the obvious shortcut

When nothing satisfies the function, `no_analogue` is the loud case and the nearest partial analogues are listed with what each one FAILS to supply. In the module's own words: relatedness is not function, which is the whole premise.
Five results, never summed
Genotype similarity, phenotype similarity, the law check, functional resolution and physics. Named, reported separately, and `cannot-assess` is not a pass.
uses: built
Refuse our own headline design
The winged zebrafish cannot leave the water: 0.67 m/s against 8.64 required, lifting area 166x too small. The film opens on it.
built
Diff a prediction against a real organism
The predicted flying zebrafish set against Exocoetus volitans, residue by residue, with a fourth colour for the columns no data covers.
built
Say which requirements cannot be assessed at all
Of 73 functional requirements, 22 were assessable and 19 of those did not resolve — 51 could not be assessed at all, most of them because the analogue side has no data. Reporting that is the product.
proposed
Validate a target function defined in TIME
Locomotion, gait, development — a phenotype that only exists as a trajectory. The harness has no time-varying target function today; every requirement it checks is a quantity at a stage.
community: A refusal you can audit
Every gate names the input it lacked, so a refusal is a to-do list rather than a verdict you must take on trust.
Bring a design, get a ledger
The output is not a score. It is a row per requirement saying assessed, unresolved, or not assessable.
The data gaps are the contribution
Nine of 3,860 genes carry a flying-fish identifier. That number is an invitation.
